caption: Are We Fast Yet's Mandelbrot, 25 laps, the same source on both: Pharo 12 (Cog) on the left, Samaltak on the right. Microseconds per lap.
spoken: Same benchmark, same source code: Pharo 12 on the left, Samaltak on the right.

caption: Samaltak is done: first lap, steady state (median of the second half) and total, in ms. Pharo is still running.
spoken: Samaltak's done. Pharo takes about three times as long.

caption: src/VM-Jit, lines per file: the baseline compiler, the optimizing compiler (Opt…), the runtime and assembler they share. Translated to C in vm/gen.
spoken: The JIT's written in Smalltalk: a baseline compiler, an optimizing one, and the runtime they share, about fourteen thousand lines. Like Pharo's Cog, it's translated to C with the rest of the VM.

caption: JitRuntime>>defaults: baseline code after 2 activations, optimized code after 1000 activations and backward jumps.
spoken: Every method starts out interpreted. Its third call compiles it with baseline, and after a thousand calls or loop iterations, opt compiles it again.

caption: Complex>>- has never run: no machine code (jitSendSites is nil). Three calls later it has baseline code; each inline cache holds the class it saw.
spoken: This one's never run, so it has no machine code. Three calls later it does, and its inline caches have recorded what they saw: Complex.

caption: Complex>>+ as baseline compiled it: the inline cache's class check at the entry, a call through each send's cache, inline SmallInteger arithmetic.
spoken: Here's baseline code for adding two complex numbers. An inline cache check on the receiver's class, a call through its own cache for each send, and inline arithmetic, with tag checks and an overflow branch.

caption: The same method from opt: class guards, inlined activations, Floats added in d registers, a deoptimization per guard. Per bytecode: 0.20 µs baseline, 3.6 µs opt (docs/jit.md).
spoken: Opt compiles it again from what those caches saw. No calls left: the accessors are inlined behind a class guard, the floats are added in FP registers, and a failed guard deoptimizes. Per bytecode, opt compiles about eighteen times slower, so only hot code gets it.

caption: MandelbrotView>>pixelFor:, inlined into the render loop: the inside of the set from black to red, ⌘S while it renders.
spoken: Opt inlined pixelFor: into the render loop. I'll make the inside of the set red, and save while it's rendering.

caption: The code that inlined it is invalidated; the running loop deoptimizes and goes on in baseline code: red from that row down. Counters before and after.
spoken: The code that inlined it gets thrown out, the running loop carries on in baseline code, and the red shows from that row down.

caption: Pharo 12's VM (libPharoVMCore.dylib): CoInterpreter and StackToRegisterMappingCogit, VMMaker's production Cogit: one machine-code method per method, sends through inline caches.
spoken: Pharo 12's VM runs Cog's StackToRegisterMappingCogit. It's the same kind of compiler as our baseline: one method at a time, and it never inlines one into another.

caption: The running system on baseline only, then on opt again (jitParameters:): ms per Mandelbrot lap. All of AWFY vs Pharo 12: baseline 0.64, opt 0.40 (docs/jit.md).
spoken: Here's the same benchmark with this system switched to baseline only, and again with opt. Across the whole suite, baseline takes sixty-four percent of Pharo's time, and opt forty.

caption: Two compilers, written in Smalltalk, live in one running image, driven through samaltak-ctl.
spoken: Two compilers, both Smalltalk, in one running image.
